paras: The killing of Ben Harris took place on August 26, 1882, near Visalia, Tulare County, California, when a Black man accused of murdering his stepdaughter and wounding his wife was shot dead by a pursuer, John Dice, while trying to escape. Harris had been hunted for four days by a party of twenty or thirty men, and wire reports of both the killings and his death ran in papers across the country.

According to a Visalia dispatch of August 22, Harris, described as "colored," shot and mortally wounded his wife about one o'clock that afternoon at their home a mile north of town and killed a 14-year-old stepdaughter. He also struck a 10-year-old stepdaughter with an ax, though the Sacramento account said she held the handle and suffered only a slight wound to the forehead. Harris fled before word reached town, and twenty or thirty men set out on his trail.

A Fresno dispatch of August 23 said Harris was armed with a shotgun and believed to be making his way north along the foothills. He instead returned during the night to the house where the killings had occurred, and his pursuers tracked him to a hiding place two and a half miles north of Visalia. There, on Saturday, August 26, he was shot fatally by John Dice while attempting to escape.
The papers do not say whether Dice held any official authority, and no report of an inquest into the shooting appears in the coverage. No later report on the condition of Harris's wife was found.

The Sacramento Daily Record-Union carried the fullest accounts, giving the time and place of the killings, the shooter's name and Harris's return to the house, without comment. A shorter wire version, headed "Negro Murderer" in the Alexandria Gazette and "Horrible Murder" in the Helena Weekly Herald, spread to papers from Seattle to Savannah and Maine within days. When Harris was killed, the Helena Weekly Herald ran the news under the heading "Got His Due," while the Daily Republican wrote that he was shot "while trying to escape arrest."

A syndicated news digest printed in Arkansas, Tennessee and elsewhere reported only that "a party of lynchers went after the murderer," with no outcome. Weekly summaries also misdated the killings to Wednesday or to "last Thursday." No Black-press coverage from 1882 is available for comparison.

reader.title: Killing of Ben Harris
bases: A party of twenty or thirty men pursued Harris after he was accused of killing family members, and four days later one of the pursuers, John Dice, shot him dead while he was 'attempting to escape' (A1, A14, A25).

Harris was killed by a member of a manhunt for an accused murderer (A14, A15), but the papers name one shooter, do not say whether Dice or the party held any authority, and describe the killing only as a shooting during an escape attempt; only a news digest calls the pursuers 'a party of lynchers' (A20).

Separate Visalia dispatches carried by the Sacramento Record-Union, the Helena Herald and a San Francisco wire agree that Harris was found near Visalia on Aug. 26 and shot while trying to escape (A14, A25, A33).

framing.detail: The Helena Herald headed the report of Harris's death 'Got His Due'.
Most papers ran the wire under headings such as 'Negro Murderer' and 'Horrible Murder' and later a one-line notice of the shooting.
The Sacramento Record-Union gave the most detail, naming the shooter and the place, without comment.
